## The tree {.i-tree-view}

The project's folder as a tree, with Catppuccin's file icons and git's
marks: a letter on a changed file, a dot on a folder with changes
inside, and ignored files dimmed. It works like a file manager: drag
files in from Finder, drag rows to move them, cut, copy, duplicate, move
to the Trash ([⌘⌫]{.kbd}) and undo ([⌘Z]{.kbd}). New File and New Folder
are at the top, and a file the agent writes appears as soon as it lands.

## Open and edit {.i-file-text}

Click a file to open it in a pane between the tree and the chat; click
it again to close it. The enlarge button gives the pane the chat's
room. [⌘S]{.kbd} saves, [⌘W]{.kbd} closes, and Emaki asks before
anything unsaved is lost. Format on save covers ten languages and is off
until you turn it on.

Code has line numbers, colors, and a gutter mark for each git change,
with a card to see or revert it. Every kind of file is drawn for what it
is:

::: {.types}
- [Code]{.i-file-code} every language, colored
- [Markdown]{.i-file-text} as it reads, or as written
- [CSV and TSV]{.i-file-table} a grid you can edit in place
- [Parquet]{.i-file-table} a table with each column's type
- [Word]{.i-file-text} pages you can type in and format
- [Excel]{.i-file-table} cells with their number formats
- [PowerPoint]{.i-file} slides as they look
- [PDF]{.i-file} sharp at any width, with search and page previews
- [HTML]{.i-file-code} in the system's web view
- [Pictures]{.i-image} at their own size
:::

## Git {.i-git-branch}

In a repository, the branch's name sits at the top of the tree. Click it
to switch branches, make one ([⌘⇧N]{.kbd}) or publish one; Fetch and
Pull are at the bottom of the list. If you switch with uncommitted
changes, Emaki asks whether to leave them or bring them along, and
switches only when every change can go where you asked.

The **Changes** pill ([⌘⇧G]{.kbd}) opens the Changes sheet: tick the
files, write the message, commit ([⌘↩]{.kbd}) and push ([⌘P]{.kbd}). A
changed picture shows before and after, side by side. **History** lists
the commits: Undo takes back the newest while the remote does not have
it, and Revert takes back any one as a new commit. Nothing is committed,
pushed or pulled until you click to do it.
